diagnosis: Customer on legacy_auth (business tier, 40 seats) asks about migration scope and rollback options. KB-0012 covers both: migration replaces account-wide tokens with scoped keys via a dual-running cutover, and is not reversible once legacy tokens are disabled. Two stable citations is common on this account and doesn't indicate related breakage.
reply: Thanks for planning ahead on this. Moving from Legacy Auth to Unified Auth replaces your account-wide token with scoped keys. The recommended approach is a dual-running window: create the scoped keys first, shift traffic over to them, and only then disable the legacy token. Because of that staging, you can revert to the legacy token at any point before you disable it — if something looks wrong during the cutover, simply keep traffic on the legacy token while you investigate. Once the legacy token is disabled, however, the migration cannot be reversed, so we suggest holding off on that final step until you're confident. Your plan includes SSO, audit log and data export, all of which continue to work under the new auth model. If you'd like, tell us your target cutover date and we can walk through the sequence with you.
